title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure the downstream effect of a deterministic network‑configuration validator plus an allowed single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter label openai_responses) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on N = 200 paired intents (completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared initial candidate passed validator checks so no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. We provide artifact‑grounded methodological detail, representative validator diagnostics, reproducibility mappings, and a focused discussion clarifying the causal limits of the executed estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics and preregistered follow‑on designs needed to measure repair efficacy under independent sampling or adversarial conditions.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are actively explored for intent→configuration workflows in network operations (NetOps). Correct translations of high‑level intent into device configuration sequences are operationally sensitive: syntactic errors, invalid command sequences, or hallucinated fields can cause redundancy loss, service disruption, or policy violations when executed. A common mitigation is a generate–validate–repair (GVR) architecture: (1) generate candidate configuration(s), (2) apply deterministic validation to detect violations against intent and topology constraints, and (3) trigger automated repair where validator failures are detected. Prior work documents verifier‑guided feedback improving correctness in related domains (e.g., infrastructure‑as‑code, program repair) and motivates applying similar pipelines to NetOps [3]. However, transferability to device‑level execution and the causal role of validators and automated repairs under different sampling semantics remain open empirical questions [4].

This study reports a fully preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment that implements the shared_initial_candidate estimand: for each intent, exactly one sampled initial generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline (no validator/repair applied) and guarded (validator applied; at most one automated repair permitted) arms. Under these semantics, any paired difference can only arise from downstream validation/repair applied to the identical candidate because per‑condition sampling variability is explicitly excluded. The paper contributes (1) an artifact‑grounded report of the executed paired experiment (N = 200 pairs) with validator traces and reconciliation; (2) exact numeric inferential results for the executed estimand showing a degenerate null effect and diagnostics explaining why repairs never executed; and (3) preregistered, artifact‑supported follow‑on estimand variants to evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling, difficulty uplift, or adversarial inputs.
sections.related_work:
Hallucination and unreliable factuality in LLM outputs are well documented and motivate grounding and verification strategies for operational tasks [1]. Retrieval‑augmented and evidence‑grounded pipelines can reduce hallucination rates in operations‑style QA but typically evaluate textual correctness rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulation [2]. Verifier‑guided architectures (generate→verify→repair) have shown empirical improvement for infrastructure‑as‑code and program generation (e.g., TerraFormer), closing the loop between generation and deterministic checks; these works motivated our approach but do not present standardized execution‑level device emulation results for NetOps in the supplied literature [3]. Recent NetOps LLM evaluations investigate intent translation and capability but lack a standardized execution‑level safety benchmark in packet‑level simulation suitable for measuring whether generator outputs would produce unsafe executable states when enacted [4].

Our study deliberately isolates the validator/repair causal path under shared_initial_candidate semantics rather than testing sampling, prompt engineering, or multi‑model generality. This narrow focus complements prior work by operationalizing a precise estimand that can be extended in preregistered follow‑on experiments to answer the broader transferability questions highlighted above.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered before any model calls (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01; preregistration SHA‑256: f0c8330d3d74cb95461d3f0291ba1b607c427ad37b5edc3750cad593bd4aae76). The primary estimand is the paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline conditions under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The design fixed task_count = 200 paired intents (planned_episode_count = 400) and allowed at most one automated repair per guarded episode; generation semantics were explicitly shared_initial_candidate so each pair reused the same sampled initial generation. Primary hypothesis H1: GVR (validator + ≤1 repair) reduces executable unsafe configurations relative to baseline on the same sampled candidate (test: exact two‑sided McNemar; alpha = 0.05). Power planning assumed an absolute risk reduction target of 10 percentage points.

Task bank, contamination checks, and selection. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed manifest of 200 synthetic "intent_configuration_repair_v1" tasks. Each manifest entry records initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotations (e.g., "safe_access_service_transfer", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and a generation_seed for deterministic replay. Prior to model calls we executed the preregistered contamination procedure (SHA‑256 exact‑match and high‑similarity n‑gram checks). No exact‑match exclusions were flagged; the confirmatory sample remained intact. Task manifest and contamination summaries are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl and analysis/contamination_summary.csv.

Generation and sampling semantics. Execution adhered to shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused in both baseline and guarded episodes. The declared generator in execution/model_configuration.json is "gpt‑5‑mini" via the hosted adapter labeled openai_responses; execution used model_calls_used = 200. The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic sampling remains possible. The provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, consistent with a single shared generation per pair.

Validator and permitted repair. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation" producing structured validator traces (validation_before, validation_after, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes) and a binary executable/invalid label. For guarded episodes a single automated repair attempt was permitted (preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline condition reused the same sampled candidate without repair; only the guarded arm could alter that same candidate via the permitted repair if validator_detections occurred. Repair provider traces (when present) and validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/*.json.

Mapping validator outputs to binary labels and analysis plan. The validator's full_intent_constraint_validation maps parsed candidate sequences and the task's required_sequence/constraints to a boolean valid flag: validator.valid = true indicates the validator judged the normalized candidate executable and compliant with required_sequence and workflow_policies. The preregistered primary statistical test is an exact two‑sided McNemar test on the 2×2 paired contingency table, supplemented by a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Missingness policy (complete_pair_primary) excludes incomplete pairs; sensitivity analysis (failure‑as‑zero) treats missing/failed episodes as unsafe. Multiplicity: single confirmatory test; exploratory subgroup tests (e.g., by difficulty level) would be corrected by Benjamini–Hochberg FDR in later analyses.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair), and completed_pair_count = 200. The analysis missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and records cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false. These reconciliation artifacts are archived in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) are baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0 for each condition). The paired contingency table (guarded vs baseline) observed n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. These analytic artifacts are archived under analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv; the bootstrap parameters and results are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Repair activity and validator diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0; no guarded episode required or invoked a repair because no shared initial candidate triggered a validator violation. Representative per‑episode JSON artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json and task‑000004‑guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate text and identical validation_after.normalized_configuration values for baseline and guarded. Example (task‑000004 shared initial excerpt): "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"; parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, validator.valid = true. Representative diagnostics for additional hard tasks (task‑000005, task‑000006) are archived and summarized in Table 2.

Contamination checks and provider audit. Preexecution contamination checks flagged no exact‑match leaks; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with one shared generation per pair. All deterministic consistency checks passed; reconciliation artifact paths and representative hashes are listed in the evidence bundle.

Interpretation of the degenerate result. The executed estimand isolates downstream validator/repair effects on fixed sampled candidates. Because all shared initial candidates were validator‑valid, the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to repair and therefore could not change outcomes. The degenerate contingency (zero discordant pairs) correctly reflects the executed estimand; it supplies no evidence about repair efficacy under independent per‑condition sampling, nor under task distributions with higher validator‑detectable failure rates.
sections.discussion:
Causal scope and design implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally remove sampling variability between conditions so that any observed paired difference is attributable solely to validator/repair applied to the identical candidate. This clarifies a causal path but narrows external claims: it does not measure whether guarded pipelines reduce generator error rates when sampling independently per condition, nor does it measure how constrained prompting or prompt templates would change first‑pass generator quality.

Threats to validity (expanded and artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: the design eliminates sampling differences by construction; this preserves internal attribution for downstream repair effects but prevents evaluation of sampling‑level interventions. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a preregistered mapping from intent constraints to checks (syntax, sequence, dependency rules, protected interfaces) and returns structured traces (validation_before/after). The validator is an abstraction: it does not run vendor CLI on physical hardware or perform packet‑level emulation; therefore timing, protocol interactions, or vendor edge‑case behaviors are not represented. External validity: the run used a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via adapter openai_responses), a synthetic deterministic task bank, and one validator implementation — generalization beyond these artifacts is unsupported by the archived evidence. Conclusion validity: the absence of discordant outcomes yields no inferential information about repair benefits under broader sampling regimes.

Operational implications and concrete follow‑on estimands. Based on archived artifacts we preregistered several follow‑on experiments that change the estimand and enable measuring repair efficacy in operationally relevant settings: (A) Independent per‑condition sampling (remove shared_initial_candidate) so baseline and guarded arms receive separate first‑pass samples—this allows repair to act on a broader set of validator‑detectable faults but conflates generation variability with repair effects and therefore requires a revised paired analysis plan; (B) Difficulty or adversary uplift: select tasks with "extreme" difficulty annotations or inject adversarial perturbations to raise expected validator failure rate and thereby exercise the repair path; (C) Explicit sampling control: set concrete temperature values (archive model_configuration.json must record non‑null temperatures) and preregister temperature sweeps to examine diversity vs validator failure tradeoffs; (D) Validator fidelity uplift: integrate vendor CLI semantics and packet‑level emulation so repairs are evaluated against dynamic runtime behavior rather than static intent constraints; (E) Multi‑model/provider sampling to assess generality across generator families. Each follow‑on design is preregistrable using the archived task bank, provider audit traces, and validator interfaces.

Why artifact grounding matters. The per‑episode JSON artifacts (execution/scoring/) contain validation_before/after subtables with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and repair_applied flags. These artifacts make transparent why repairs did not execute in this run and allow independent reanalysis of the executed estimand without ambiguity about sampling semantics or hidden retries. The execution/model_configuration.json explicitly records declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini" and temperature = null; as stated earlier, null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. The master prompt immutable reference is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is reported in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment designed to measure the downstream effect of deterministic validation and an allowed single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). With gpt‑5‑mini declared as the generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the scorer, every shared initial candidate passed validation and no repairs were attempted or applied; guarded and baseline outcomes were identical for the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This artifact‑grounded null result demonstrates an estimand boundary: under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the task bank sampled here, the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to change the outcome. It does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary in general. As preregistered and archived, follow‑on experiments that (1) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics, (2) increase task difficulty or inject adversarial inputs, (3) set explicit sampling parameters, and (4) raise validator fidelity are required to empirically evaluate repair efficacy under realistic sampling variability and adversarial conditions. The archived artifacts and reconciliation files enable exact reproduction of the executed estimand and provide a secure base for precise preregistered extensions.

(Reviewer‑requested clarifications included here) We explicitly reiterate that the primary estimand was intentionally limited by shared_initial_candidate semantics: independent per‑condition sampling would constitute a different preregistered estimand and analytical plan and is therefore not assessed by the present execution. Finally, Table 3 below lists the one‑line repair summary requested by reviewers (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise): The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) prior to the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, experiment selection, preregistration (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01; preregistration SHA‑256: f0c8330d3d74cb95461d3f0291ba1b607c427ad37b5edc3750cad593bd4aae76), code generation, execution, deterministic validation, automated analysis, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model used in execution: gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter 'openai_responses' (execution used model_calls_used = 200; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Generation semantics executed: shared_initial_candidate — exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded conditions (no independent per‑condition first‑pass sampling). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored candidates using 'full_intent_constraint_validation' and a single automated repair iteration was permitted in guarded episodes; in this run the validator flagged no violations and no repairs were applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Execution accounting: completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired intents) completed without preregistration deviations; execution manifest and analysis artifacts are archived under execution/* and analysis/*. Master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred but pre‑lock artifacts were not used as empirical evidence in this final run. After the autonomy lock no human manually rewrote technical results, manuscript text, figures, or references.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
